approach: Correct implementation drift against a spec that is already right: workflows/detect-and-repair already states that an owner cannot always be read off the report and that routing is on problem. The shipped repair SKILL.md says the opposite.
Replace the family split with membership in references/classes.md, keyed by problem — the one rule that holds for all twenty-seven problems and fails safe on the twenty-eighth.

Re-count the issue's table against the tree: it predates both the command/instruction split and the MCP family, so its counts are stale even though its diagnosis holds. Say so rather than repeating them.
Settle the replacement wording by running cold agents over the current and candidate text against a doctor report, rather than by argument.
Revise one spec node (skills/repair) whose own routing sentence contradicts the seam node; change nothing on the seam node itself.
blast-radius: prose only — one shipped skill body, its reference file, one spec node and its suite, one docs page. No source module, no published API, no generated artifact.

what: doctor's unloadable-skill detail hedges between the two faults that arrive under that name — 'frontmatter that does not parse, or no description' — but the repair skill's correction reference separates them into a correctable quoting fault and a non-correctable missing description that must be reported and asked about instead. The finding therefore cannot say which correction applies, and the skill is told to route on problem and never on detail, so the distinction is reachable only by opening the file. Either the problem name splits in two or the finding carries which fault it found.
where: cli/configuration-diagnosis, the node that owns the check
evidence: three of six blind sorting runs raised it unprompted as the one thing they could not resolve from the report

what: The help section carries no key back to the finding it repairs. It follows findings order and collapses only an identical repair, so position works, but nothing in the reported data states that — a consumer either infers the correspondence or scans the instruction prose for a path, which ties when two findings sit at one path. A key field, or a stated ordering guarantee, would make the pairing readable rather than inferred.
where: cli/diagnosis-report, the node that owns the output shape
evidence: two independent blind runs hit the same tie on two findings at one bridge path

why: Two judge rounds. Round one returned blocked on a governance pre-flight failure - the dispatch declared an empty set, which was accurate, and the block was correct; that round also asserted a plugin squad for this artifact-type, which the matcher does not support. Resolved the chain against the project registry (every bar plugin-null, pure SDD default), loaded the three spec-gate actor bars and both format bars, self-aligned, re-dispatched cold. Round two passed pre-flight and all three backward lenses, with an adversarial factual cross-check against the guidance table and the report assembly confirming every claim in the diff: twenty-seven problems across four families, a skill named in the command rendering for eight of them and none of the nineteen bridge and MCP problems, four sections in the correction reference matching the new membership remit, and the help dedup key and ordering matching the sentence describing them. Both flagged points resolved non-blocking. Deterministic checks clean: spec-state, suite, scenario-overlap, spec-structure. Suite frozen at feature level, matching the two most recently gated nodes in this corpus. Self-asserted within the derived auto-all leash.

what: The repair node's control-flow graph has no explicit per-finding routing node. Node A is the single run-the-command action, and the scenario asserting that two findings at one path are told apart by their own repairs is attributed to it for want of a better edge, which reads loose. A per-finding dispatch node between the any-finding check and the remit check would give that scenario, and the family-guard scenarios, an edge that names what they actually test.
evidence: raised as an architect observation by the cold spec-judge at this CR's spec gate; non-blocking there

why: Two rounds. Round one failed one of the twenty-two frozen scenarios and was correct: the shipped handoff rule asked whether a repair named the init skill, but six of the nine bridge repairs render a runnable init command line and name the skill nowhere, so a rebuildable bridge routed to a person against the scenario that hands it to init. The explore evidence could not have caught it - the fixture's only bridge fault was one of the three a rebuild would not fix, so eight blind runs never saw the case. Rebuilt the fixture with a degraded bridge and reproduced the misroute on the pre-fix text before accepting the finding. Declined the remediation round one proposed, which would have put a hand-kept list of rebuild-fixable problems into the shipped text - the maintained-list failure this change request exists to remove, and unreadable from the report; asked instead whether the repair names init in either form, which the report answers on its face. Round two passed all twenty-two by static inspection, independently re-derived the ten-thirteen-four partition by hand before checking the new test's array, confirmed the test reads the same function the command renders help from, and cleared the absorption and structural reads. Self-asserted within the derived auto-all leash.

what: The init-handoff rule is hand-authored twice in near-identical prose, in the repair skill body and in its correction reference. The underlying table is now test-pinned, but the two prose copies are not pinned to each other, so a future edit to one can silently diverge from the other. Currently consistent. This is the codebase's general skill-body-summarizes, reference-elaborates pattern rather than anything new here, so the fix is a pattern-level decision about how shipped skill prose is kept in sync, not a local edit.
where: skills/repair, and the shipped-skill prose pattern generally
evidence: raised as an architect observation by the cold impl-judge at this CR's impl gate; non-blocking there
